findings.title: Mutable default value `timezone.now()` evaluated once at class definition time
findings.body: The default value `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is first imported, not at each instance creation. This means every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` argument will share the same stale timestamp from import time. The correct pattern is `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)` (importing `field` from `dataclasses`). While the `queued` field isn't currently used for logic, it's serialized via `to_dict()` and passed through task kwargs, so any downstream consumer or future time-based logic (e.g., TTL, ordering, debugging) will see incorrect timestamps.

findings.title: Passing `assignment_source` kwarg to `sync_assignee_outbound` may break concrete implementations without `**kwargs`
findings.body: The call `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign, assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` passes `assignment_source` as a keyword argument. While the abstract method signature includes `**kwargs`, any concrete integration implementation that overrides `sync_assignee_outbound` with a fixed parameter list (no `**kwargs`) will raise a `TypeError` at runtime. This is a potential backward-compatibility break for third-party or less common integration implementations.

findings.title: `from_dict` does not handle non-datetime `queued` values from deserialization
findings.body: When `AssignmentSource` is round-tripped through `to_dict()` and `from_dict()` (as happens via Celery task kwargs), the `queued` field will be a string (ISO format) rather than a `datetime` object. The dataclass constructor does not enforce types, so `from_dict` will silently produce an instance with a string `queued` field. If any code later compares or operates on `queued` as a datetime, it will fail. Consider parsing the `queued` field in `from_dict` or excluding it from serialization if it's not needed downstream.

findings.title: Test does not verify that `queued` reflects instance creation time
findings.body: The `test_to_dict` test only asserts `result.get('queued') is not None`, which passes even with the stale module-level `timezone.now()` default. A test creating two instances at different times and asserting their `queued` values differ (or that `queued` is close to `timezone.now()` at creation time) would catch the default-value bug.
